 Irish tax revenue up 10% so far this year
 A woman walks through Temple Bar, in Dublin, Ireland, February 18, 2025. REUTERS/Clodagh Kilcoyne · Reuters Reuters Wed, November 4, 2026 at 10:38 AM CST 1 min read AAPL +5.17%

 Learn more DUBLIN, Nov 4 (Reuters) - Ireland's tax revenue rose 10.3% in the first 10 months ‌of 2026 compared to a year ‌earlier, excluding one-off proceeds from a ruling related to Apple ​back taxes, the finance ministry said on Wednesday. 
 A surge in corporate tax paid mainly by a small group of US multinationals has helped ‌drive overall tax ⁠revenue to record levels each year since 2021 and handed the government ⁠large budget surpluses to spend and save. 
 Receipts are forecast to grow by another 5% on an ​underlying basis ​this year, with ​income tax and VAT ‌returns, which were 8% and 7% higher respectively at the end of October, also contributing strongly. 
 While corporate tax receipts are up 23% so far this year compared to the same period ‌in 2025, that is ​partly due to early payments ​that the ​finance ministry expect to even out ‌by year-end. 
 Government spending was up ​7.4% year-on-year ​by the end of last month, the data showed, with expenditure on day-to-day services ​again growing ‌at a faster pace than major planned ​investments in public infrastructure. 
 (Reporting by Padraic Halpin; ​editing by William James)
